description.narrative: 1. In April 2023, the MOLE-BARMM (Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao) formalized the creation of a Child Labour Protection Unit (CLPU). Prior to this, in 2022, in anticipation of the creation of the CLPU, a budget was allocated for the unit's 2023 activities. 2. The National Council Against Child Labor (NCACL) adopted the Program Against Child Labour Strategic (PPACL) Framework 2023 – 2028 on March 2023 . An NCACL Council Resolution was issued on 5 September 2023 to formally approve the PPACL Actional 2023-2028. 1. With support from the Government of Japan, the ILO conducted several awareness-raising activities/meetings with and orientation of MOLE-BARMM, specifically the Bureau of Employment Promotions and Welfare. In March 2023, the ILO conducted an orientation on the importance of a child labour unit in response to MOLE-BEPW's request to capacitate the Ministry on the importance and roles and responsibilities of a child labour unit. 2. With support from the Government of Japan, the ILO provided technical assistance to the NCACL in conducting several consultations for the drafting of the PPACL Strategic Framework and its Action Plan in December 2022 and April 2023, respectively. 3. The ILO, with support from the Government of Japan, provided technical assistance and supported the BARMM government in conducting consultations and interviews from February 2021 to March 2022 for the drafting of the Bangsamoro Regional Action Plan on Child Labour (BRAP-CL). It is envisioned that the BRAP-CL will be adopted in 2023.

description.narrative: In 2023, the Ministry of Labor and Employment (MOLE) in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) started implementing its Strategic Action Plan for 2023-2030. The MOLE Strategic Action Plan is the anchor of planning and embodies the Ministry's vision, development goals, objectives, strategies and policies with corresponding programmes, projects, and activities, including the implementation in line with MOLE’s 2023- 2030 vision of a “decent, competitive, productive and sustainable employment in the Bangsamoro.” The ILO supported MOLE in the drafting of the Strategic Action Plan BARMM. The ILO also provided technical inputs to the discussions through the Labour Market and Labour Administration Assessments as well as in the conduct of a series of workshops and capacity building activities for MOLE.

description.narrative:
In March 2023, the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) issued a memo institutionalizing the Strategic Compliance Plans (SCP) developed by each of its 16 Regional Offices to guide its inspection activities and support convergence of programmes towards compliance to labour standards.
These Strategic Compliance Plans (SCP) of each region targeted specific violations, especially OSH hazards and risks, and sectors not traditionally covered by the labour inspectorate. Thus, the plans combine a number of strategies apart from labour inspection, which can support compliance, such as delivery of technical advisory services, incentive programmes, collaboration with other government bodies and stakeholders. With the support of the US Department of Labor, ILO supported DOLE in the design and facilitation of the Planning Workshop for the Regional Directors, and even during the follow up workshops involving the Provincial and Field Directors. Prior to this, the ILO supported its pilot regions in the development of Industry Tripartite Sectoral Compliance Plans, where its partner workers and employers’ organisations also made their own commitments on how they can contribute to the promotion of labour standards compliance. This exercise gave DOLE and some regions a better appreciation of the process, and how this can be applied to the labour inspectorate in general.
